headline: Join the US Coast Guard: 2026 Enlistment and Officer Guide
metaDescription: US Coast Guard recruitment 2026: age 17-42, AFQT 40 minimum, 8-week boot camp at Cape May, OCS and Academy officer paths, ratings and pay from E-1 upward.

sections.content:
The United States Coast Guard is the maritime branch of the US armed forces, but unlike the other services it operates under the Department of Homeland Security in peacetime. Its missions span search and rescue, maritime law enforcement, port security, drug interdiction, environmental protection and coastal defense, with authority in both domestic and international waters.

Because it is the smallest armed service, the Coast Guard is historically the hardest branch to enter, with limited intake quotas each year. Recruitment runs through local Coast Guard recruiters, and the process includes the ASVAB, a MEPS medical exam, background and credit checks, and an English comprehension requirement for non-native speakers.
sections.title: The Coast Guard Mission and Force Overview

sections.content:
Enlisted applicants must be 17 to 42 years old, with parental consent required at 17. You must be a US citizen or a legal permanent resident with fluent English, and hold a high school diploma or GED equivalent. The service will also check personal conduct, criminal history and alcohol or drug abuse records.

The Coast Guard publishes the highest AFQT minimum of any branch: 40 for diploma holders and 50 for GED holders. Each rating, the Coast Guard's term for a military job, carries its own ASVAB line-score minimums, so higher scores unlock more career options. Fitness benchmarks include pushups, a forearm plank hold and a 1.5-mile run.
sections.title: Enlisted Eligibility: Age, Citizenship and ASVAB

sections.content:
Every enlisted recruit ships to Training Center Cape May in New Jersey for an 8-week boot camp, the only basic training site in the service, where men and women train together under one regimen. The course blends physical conditioning, drill, classroom instruction in military justice and Coast Guard history, plus hands-on seamanship, damage control, firefighting, firearms and water survival training.

Graduation takes place on Fridays at 11:00 AM after the final week, with families able to attend. After boot camp, graduates proceed to their first unit or to A-school for rating-specific technical training, with some ratings offering guaranteed school slots before shipping.
sections.title: Boot Camp at Cape May: The 8-Week Course

sections.content:
Officers follow a different path than enlisted recruits. The US Coast Guard Academy in New London, Connecticut offers a free four-year undergraduate program with degrees in fields like civil engineering, naval architecture and operations research, commissioning officers upon graduation. College graduates and prior-enlisted members can instead attend Officer Candidate School, an intensive 12-week course also held at New London.

Pay matches the other services: a 2026 E-1 earns $2,407 per month basic pay after the first four months, rising with grade and seniority, plus tax-free BAH and BAS allowances, health care, 30 days of annual leave and tuition assistance. Commissioned officers start around $4,150 per month as ensigns.
